expected.claim: completeCopyrightFormScreening takes the notice FOR KEY SHARE and then inserts the screening, whose AFTER trigger upserts the case generation row. acceptCopyrightNoticeAndImposeRestriction takes the generation FOR UPDATE and then the notice FOR UPDATE. Copyright counter-notice reviews, appeal reviews, assessment appends, restriction admission, and screening completion stop acquiring redundant advisory locks. Existing written-row locks and conditional writes govern their state changes.

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Counter-notice or appeal review | Submission-key advisory before written-row locks | Existing generation and notice locks protect review state and effects |
| Assessment or restriction admission | Extra form lookup and advisory lock | Existing generation lock precedes assessment authority reads |
| Screening restart or completion | Re-entered the form advisory | Restart uses its caller's existing advisory; completion uses the written attempt lock and lease predicates |
| Concurrent identical counter-notice reviews | Serialized by advisory and row locks | Return the same result and persist one review and deadline under existing written-row locks |

## Impact

Copyright review and screening requests avoid the removed advisory acquisitions. API results and review effects are preserved. Recovery remains unchanged by the user's explicit decision; its lock-order work stays open under #6015 and #5253.

title: refactor(users): narrow account-deletion fence callers
reason: Pilot verdict at this head found 1 real defect(s), first: voter fence replaced by in-INSERT EXISTS(users deleted_at IS NULL): a ballot committed after a concurrent account deletion survives with ip/device/session data; at least one is reasoned only (no later head fixed it). The full review run at this head reported 1 of the 1 expected findings.

expected.claim: The ballot INSERT checks that the user is not deleted inside the statement, on the statement snapshot. The foreign key takes KEY SHARE on the users row, which does not wait for the deletion transaction's FOR NO KEY UPDATE, so a deletion that commits mid transaction is missed. The deletion's votes phase cannot see the uncommitted ballot, so the ballot with ip, device and session data outlives the deleted user. Keep the voter fence (FOR SHARE on the users row) on the ballot upserts.

body:
## Summary

The account-deletion fence locks user rows for ballots, classifier work and staff writes. Remove those pre-write locks and check active users in the affected writes or actor reads.

## Impact

Ballot submissions, classifier jobs, moderator restriction changes and staff role grants no longer take these user-row locks. Credential, session and other personal-data writes keep their deletion fences.

## Related issues

- Refs #6034 — Audits and narrows the active-user deletion fence callers.
Partial batch; source issue remains open for remaining work.
<!-- related-issues-validation: partial-batch -->

## Details

| Path | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent-moderation and entity-relation ballots | Lock the voter's user row before appending | Only append while the voter is active in the insert statement's snapshot |
| Classifier decisions and runs | Take a shared system actor's deletion fence | Check the active actor without locking the user row |
| Story clustering reservations | Fence the shared actor before checking the feed item | Reuse the existing item read and resolve the system actor through configuration |
| Community restriction writes | Fence the acting moderator’s user row | Check the active actor in each restriction write |
| Staff role grants | Take two locks on the target user row | Check the target’s active status in the role insert and vote-weight update |

## Concurrency

Both ballot inserts check the active voter inside the statement that appends the ballot. Aggregation still consumes each voter's latest ballot. Classifier run execution checks the actor in the run query and locks only the run through that statement. The staff role grant keeps its existing serializable transaction for administrator grants and checks the active user in both writing statements. Personal-data producers still take the account-deletion fence before writing data that deletion must collect.

title: Gate repeated generic-plan execution slowdowns
reason: Pilot verdict at this head found 1 real defect(s), first: generic-plan regression gate passes silently when zero query pairs are compared, so a dropped compare mode disables it unnoticed; at least one is reasoned only (no later head fixed it). The full review run at this head reported 0 of the 1 expected findings.

expected.claim: assertNoGenericPlanRegressions only compares pairs captured in compare mode. If EXPLAIN_PLAN_CACHE_MODE=compare is dropped from the job, no pairs exist and the gate passes with nothing checked. Throw when zero pairs were compared, and cover the call with a test.

body:
## Summary

The EXPLAIN analyzer accepted a generic prepared plan that took 245 times as long as the custom plan. Compare corresponding custom and generic captures and fail a statement when the slowdown exceeds 10× and adds more than 200 ms in both capture passes.

Match captures by scenario, input ordinal, operation name, exact SQL and JIT mode so repeated statements and different input sets cannot be mixed. Keep the existing physical-work and resource gates.

Refs #6043

## Impact

CI now blocks sustained, substantial generic-plan regressions before PostgreSQL can choose those plans for prepared statements. This changes EXPLAIN analysis only. The active-relation fix in #6047 and the pruning fix in #6080 are merged into main. This PR is based on main.

## Before and after

The gate replays the merged artifacts from [CI run 44979310144](https://github.com/vouchington/vouchington/actions/runs/44979310144). The artifacts include 2,666 captures for 1,333 statement pairs per pass. The SQL and captured plans are identical in both analyzer runs.

| Archived scenario | Custom → generic, first | Custom → generic, repeat | Before | With gate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| Story active related URLs, maximum | 23.739 → 5,803.190 ms (244.5×) | 23.666 → 5,926.598 ms (250.4×) | Passed | Failed |
| Critical alert batch insert | 5,564.513 → 597.061 ms | 5,082.239 → 408.645 ms | Passed | Passed |
| Story projection receipt insert, maximum | 1,777.645 → 225.042 ms | 1,715.401 → 221.729 ms | Passed | Passed |

The story generic plan repeated an aggregate under a nested loop and discarded 49,995,000 pairs in its join filter. It was the only archived statement this gate rejected. All 138 statement pairs with trigger timings in their generic captures passed.

The gate checks for a generic plan above 10× the custom execution time and over 200 ms of added execution in both passes. The absolute margin uses the slow-capture scale in #6043 and keeps short queries away from the timing noise near zero. The repeat distinguishes sustained slowdowns from a single cold capture. In that archived run, the story prune and heavy post-feed regressions add at least 173.505 ms and 58.726 ms respectively across both passes and are below this gate's cutoff. A later CI run exceeded the unchanged gate for pruning in both captures; #6080 fixes that separate defect tracked by #6077.

The gate protects user-facing and background queries against multi-second regressions that may appear after PostgreSQL switches prepared plan modes. #6047 fixes the active-relation lookup and #6080 fixes pruning. Both SQL fixes have merged into main.

## Limits

A single-pass outlier or a short query below the absolute margin does not fail this gate. Unmatched custom/generic pairs are not compared. Existing capture validation and the other analysis gates continue to apply.

title: refactor(memberships): remove four redundant row locks
reason: Pilot verdict at this head found 1 real defect(s), first: apple lineage FOR UPDATE removed: two family verifications on one user and lineage can now deadlock on the family source and the users vote-weight UPDATE; at least one is reasoned only (no later head fixed it). The full review run at this head reported 0 of the 1 expected findings.

expected.claim: The existing-lineage read is now unlocked, so two Apple family verifications for the same user and lineage both proceed. Each takes FOR SHARE on the users row; one locks the family source and the other waits holding its share lock, and then the first needs the users row for its vote-weight UPDATE and waits on the second. That is a deadlock main could not produce because the lineage lock queued them first. Restore the lock on the lineage read.

body:
## Summary

Stripe cancellation returns `completed: true` when a competing worker already finished it. Refund scan completion succeeds when its fallback read finds the requested generation already complete.

Remove four redundant row locks from elapsed grant expiry, Apple lineage reads, Stripe cancellation lookup, and the refund-scan completion fallback. Keep the provider-source lock so each observation projects against the preceding committed state.

## Impact

Expiry still updates the uniquely bounded current projection. Apple binding retains its conditional write and owner check. A newer Apple or Google expiration advances entitlement state after a concurrent renewal commits. Family projection uses the same user-deletion check and SHARE lock as main.

## Related issues

- Refs #6034 — Audits memberships and Stripe; other service groups and the explicitly listed privacy and unresolved sites still require owner review.
Partial batch; source issue remains open for remaining work.
<!-- related-issues-validation: partial-batch -->

## Details

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Grant expiry | Prelocked a uniquely bounded current projection | Updates the eligible projection directly |
| Apple verification lineage read | Locked the lineage before validation and binding | The conditional ownership write and a fresh read identify the winning account |
| Provider observation projection | Source lock serializes observations before the state upsert | Main’s source lock is retained so the next state upsert sees the preceding observation |
| Cancellation completion race | Lookup lock serialized the claim | Failed claim rereads completion |

### Concurrency

Family projection retains the shared user fence from main. Two advancing family projections for one user can still deadlock when both try to upgrade the shared lock to update the vote-weight marker. In the Apple and Google concurrency regression, a newer expiration waits for an uncommitted renewal and then updates the source observation and expires the membership. Removing the source lock reproduces the stale renewal and leaves the membership active.

The expiry statement keeps every existing eligibility predicate on the row it updates. Only its RETURNING rows close source/activation state and produce history. Concurrent binders still need the provider binding unique index and the existing compare-and-set conditions. The first binder owns the row, and a contender reuses it only if the fresh owner matches. The refund-cycle registration lock remains for owner decision. A serializable registration/completion experiment rejected the intended write skew, but parallel tests on distinct reversal cases also received 40001. EXPLAIN on the disposable database showed sequential scans of the cycle and scan ledgers for the exact case predicates, extending SSI dependencies across cases at this cardinality.

| Site | Class | Action and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `memberships/lock-user.mts` · `lockMembershipUser` → `fn_lock_active_user_for_mutation` | P | Keep existing deletion fence. The function reads users by ID, rejects a missing row or non-null deleted_at, and waits on deletion's users write lock before validating. |
| `memberships/create/persist.mts` · `createMembershipWithQuery` | P | Keep existing SHARE for durable grant, Stripe source/binding and projection writes. This creates only admin-grant/direct sources; even expiry and fallback do not update users. |
| `memberships/provider-observation-projection-source.mts` · direct observations | P | Keep existing SHARE, fencing new verified provider binding/entitlement writes against account deletion. |
| `memberships/provider-observation-projection-source.mts` · family observations | P/W | Keep the same SHARE fence as main. An advancing family source calls markVoteWeightDirtyInTransaction. A stale observation can exit without an update. |
| `stripe/membership-sync/sync-or-create.mts` · `syncOrCreateStripeMembershipInTransaction` | P | Keep existing SHARE. The outer entry covers reconciliation/collision ledger paths and may call createMembershipWithQuery, which also protects independent creation entry points. Neither path updates users. |
| `memberships/grants/expire-elapsed-page.mts` | W0 | Remove projection CTE/lock. The same predicate runs in UPDATE and the unique effective-user index allows one current row. |
| `memberships/grants/revoke.mts` | ? | Keep pending owner decision. The lock currently serializes revocations; the service reads cross-row activation/remaining time and projects fallback only for an active grant. The conditional revoked_at update alone cannot preserve the active branch on a concurrent activation; the losing revocation also needs a fresh replay result. |
| `memberships/provider-source.mts` · existing source | R | By explicit owner direction, keep main’s `FOR UPDATE` on the source before state projection. Rebinding uses the UPDATE RETURNING row while the source row is held. Waiting inside the upsert can expose a new state row version while its observation lookup still uses the old statement snapshot. |
| `memberships/apple/process-verification-finalize.mts` · lineage | R/W0 | Remove explicit lineage lock. Family reads the lineage ID. Direct conditional binding permits only NULL → token and rereads a losing claim; the immutable-lineage trigger forbids subsequent account changes. |
| `memberships/apple/process-verification-context.mts` · verification | W | Keep pending verification row lock, which guards distinct verification workflows through eventual finalize and observation/projection writes. |
| `memberships/apple/process-verification-context.mts` · evidence | ? | Keep for owner decision. Some branches replay prior evidence (read only), others bind or reject the evidence; evidence can also be finalized independently by Apple notification with a different claim. |
| `memberships/apple/notification-context.mts` · evidence | W | Keep evidence lock for the observation and verified/rejected terminal transition on the same evidence row. |
| `memberships/google/verification-context.mts` · verification and evidence | ? | Keep for owner decision. The shared context is used by read-only fetch/preflight branches and by rejecting, pending-source, terminalization and verified branches. A common removal needs separate treatment for evidence replay, conditional finalization and a one-winner Google acknowledgement. |
| `memberships/ineligible-stripe-purchase-cancellation.mts` · operation lookup | W0 | Remove lookup lock; the execution claim already locks the same operation and checks completion and lease validity. Read completion again when the guarded claim returns no lease, preserving completed replay if another worker finished after the first read. |
| `memberships/operation-execution-work.mts` · execution claim | W | Keep. Claim and completion trigger both write operation and work. Locking operation first prevents an operation/work order inversion and avoids clearing a completed operation's work. |
| `memberships/ineligible-stripe-purchase-reversal/target-ledger.mts` · reversal operation | W | Keep where the locked amount/receipt/failure read drives reconciliation and the subsequent operation update and lease claim. |
| `memberships/ineligible-stripe-purchase-reversal/won-dispute-recovery-operations.mts` · recovery operation | W | Keep where locked amount/failure/receipt reads drive reconciliation or completion and a subsequent claim. |
| `memberships/ineligible-stripe-purchase-reversal/refund-scan-cycle-ledger.mts` · get/rotate cycle | W | Keep cycle lock to choose the active generation or rotate a completed row once and return the selected generation. |
| Same file · completion fallback | R | Remove final read lock. The preceding UPDATE handles idempotent completion; the fallback only checks whether this generation already completed. |
| Same file · register target against active cycle | ? | Keep for owner decision. Registration reads the active cycle then writes a scan. Completion writes the cycle after checking for unverified scans. The parent lock cannot refresh an older completion statement snapshot. SERIALIZABLE prevents this write skew, but the experiment produced 40001s on unrelated case IDs in parallel tests. A narrower replay read did not remove that contention. |
| Same file · getStripeRefundScanLocked | W/? | Keep for owner decision on registration. Applying scan pages reads generation, cursor, head and timestamps and appends observations plus writes the same scan. Registration may return an already registered scan, or it may update registration/reset fields through ON CONFLICT. The lookup after upsert already holds the write lock. |
| `memberships/pause-collection/dispatch.mts` · unleased / expired claims | Q | Keep both SKIP LOCKED claims on written work rows. Scheduled, operator and user-triggered dispatch can overlap; enqueue deduplication does not exclude distinct jobs or stalled redelivery. |
| `memberships/entitlement-effects.mts` · effect claim | Q | Keep SKIP LOCKED on written effect rows. Bucketed wakeups and scheduled recovery can overlap. |
| `memberships/refund-reconciliation/dispatcher.mts` · due operations | Q | Keep SKIP LOCKED on written operations. Scheduled and manual dispatch can overlap a direct executor, with operation-first ordering shared by completion. |
| `memberships/refund-reconciliation/ledger.mts` · retry scheduling | W | Keep operation-first ordering with completion and its work deletion trigger; retry updates both operation and work. |
| `stripe/membership-provider-facts/observation.mts` · current Stripe observation state | W | Keep source-state lock. Ordering and terminal/rejected observation checks determine the later write of the same state row. |

## Summary

Concurrent moderation inserts can miss each other and strand superseded rows without a retention due date. Publish one-time reconciliation work on each result through its existing retention fields, then drain ordinary due work in a fresh transaction.

## Impact

Superseded moderations become eligible even when inserts commit out of ID order or a prior cleanup marked the older result newest. Settled keepers leave the work index, so idle cleanup does not revisit them. Existing keeper, hash, reference, age and owned-post deletion guards remain.

## Related issues

- Closes #6037 — Repairs missed retention due dates after concurrent inserts, with bounded recovery in the existing cleanup job.

## Details

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Concurrent or out-of-order inserts | Trigger snapshots can leave a predecessor with no due date | Each inserted result retains its own reconciliation work until committed-state reconciliation |
| Settled newest predecessor | A missed wake can leave it retained indefinitely | A later result reconciles its keyed predecessors, including newest-blocked results |
| Idle settled keepers | Recurring repair scan walks them on every pass | Settled rows have no due work and leave the work index |
| Batch size one | Final-slot reservation processes no due rows | One shared candidate page processes the full configured batch |
| Durable production path | Test-only override enables the repair cursor | Public cleanup consumes real persisted row state; obsolete repair cursor and override are removed |

### One-time work and concurrency

The current producer publishes pending reconciliation using existing retention fields on the source row. No table, column, explicit lock or per-post coordination write is added. Reconciliation converts pending work into ordinary due work; it never classifies a pending result as newest. A separate ordinary cleanup transaction acquires the original source lock and evaluates deletion guards with a fresh statement snapshot.

A newer pending result leaves a pending predecessor intact, so the predecessor can still reconcile its own earlier results. Wakes of ordinary due or newest-blocked predecessors are conditional writes. Lifecycle changes republish pending work and are checked before consuming a captured source. These rules stand independently of queue scheduling: a stalled delivery can overlap its original invocation.

### Bounds and query evidence

Candidate pages use the existing due index and continuation shape. Both batch_size and max_batches_per_run are clamped to their DATA_RETENTION_MAX_VALUES hard limits. There is no reserved final slot and no periodic keeper-repair cursor. Reconciliation takes only keyed predecessor probes for its bounded source page.

On the production-sized PostgreSQL 18 fixture, the plain source join visited 1,101 moderation tuples through a bitmap heap scan for 100 candidates. The keyed LATERAL form uses 100 exact composite-key source probes and 100 exact target probes. It preserves the physical read bound under skew; this is not a speed claim (the measured keyed form took about 2.13/2.46 ms versus 1.75/2.21 ms for the plain form).

Custom and generic plans leave the future partition unexecuted for source, predecessor and target probes. Active due selection returns the existing 101-row page-plus-lookahead through the due index; the settled idle selection returns zero rows with five shared hits. The idle EXPLAIN scenario requires that settled keepers are not visited. Existing numeric row, sort and index gates remain enforced.

### Schema publication and validation limits

The canonical schema changes are limited to agent-moderation retention: inserts and lifecycle changes publish one-time work through existing fields; the recurring repair index and cursor kind are removed.

The five changed generated files come from [trusted PostgreSQL 18 workflow run 45014530024](https://github.com/vouchington/vouchington/actions/runs/45014530024), bound to source `78895b474386c661efdb53d0d47f385639bfcd77` and base `664d8dd83d12713d962734aa1afb442744448c81`. Generation succeeded; only publication failed with the existing [HTTPS credential problem #6054](https://github.com/vouchington/vouchington/issues/6054). The canonical manifest/inventory/SHA-256 validator checked all 595 artifact files and live PR identity before applying only changed output through the canonical destination mapper. Manifest digest: `cf873d8b9699302413339591138201116f5f058344a9013871a3a681e45a04f9`.

The reviewed output is committed at `53d4183787405265a7432858a9a7fef056d6e50c`, directly atop the generated source. Normal backend initialization, live-schema verification, and the full catalog comparison under CI's UTC session convention passed on that source/output pair.

Local direct captures do not cover the full EXPLAIN harness function-counter gates because the disposable role cannot set track_functions. The registered CI scenarios retain their existing gates.

### Native stack

This is the bottom of native stack #6088. The upper [#6078](https://github.com/vouchington/vouchington/pull/6078) contains the separate #6034 moderation lock audit. Its original source locks and child-FK protections remain. The upper branch is rebased through the native stack after the lower implementation is finalized.

### CI verification gap

[Backend EXPLAIN run 45015031835](https://github.com/vouchington/vouchington/actions/runs/45015031835) on `53d4183787405265a7432858a9a7fef056d6e50c` exposed an overly narrow posts-index expectation in the deletion scenario's forced generic plan. ## Summary

Concurrent moderation inserts can leave a superseded result without `retention_due_at`. Add an age-bounded repair phase to the existing cleanup run, checkpoint its position through the existing retention cursor mechanism, and bound each scheduled run with the existing `maxBatches`.

## Impact

Overdue superseded agent moderations become eligible for deletion after overlapping inserts. Keeper-only ranges now generate bounded repair continuations, increasing cleanup work on otherwise idle sweeps. Existing keeper, hash, age, reference and owned-post rules still govern deletion.

## Related issues

- Closes #6037 — Repairs missed retention due dates after concurrent inserts, with bounded recovery in the existing cleanup job.

## Details

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Adjacent concurrent inserts | A superseded row can retain a NULL due date indefinitely | Bounded repair stamps eligible superseded results; the existing prelocked due path removes them |
| Keeper-only aged range | Each daily run restarts the repair scan | The next run resumes the last inspected `(id, post_id)` and its frozen upper bound |
| Sustained due backlog | Due work can consume the whole repair budget | The final daily batch reserves one repair slot within its existing batch size |
| Due continuation | Carries a repair position through an unbounded continuation chain | Drains due work only; repair stays within the scheduled run's existing `maxBatches` |
| End of repair pass | Repair progress only exists in a queue payload | Clear the persisted cursor and stop repair for this run; the next run starts a new pass |

### Implementation choice

Keep the indexed due drain and insert triggers. Add a partial `(id, post_id)` index for NULL-due, unblocked rows and use keyed successor probes in a conditional UPDATE. The age-bounded repair SELECT uses a maximum visible post ID to prune future partitions; the foreign key to `posts ON DELETE CASCADE` makes that bound complete for visible rows, including soft-deleted posts.

The cleanup-time derivation alternative filtered 100,000 keepers before returning 101 candidates in a PostgreSQL 18.6 synthetic partitioned EXPLAIN, exceeding the inspected-row bound. The final production-schema capture retains indexed due selection, the original keyed source lock and index-only repair selection without sorting. Existing numeric EXPLAIN budgets remain unchanged.

### Concurrency and bounded progress

No new explicit lock, coordination column or table is added. A distinct `agent_moderation_repair` kind uses existing `post_moderation_retention_cursors` fields for the last inspected moderation ID, its post-ID tie-breaker, and the frozen age upper bound. Repair and checkpoint commit together on the existing single-flight retention lane. A short page resets the persisted pass and stops repair for the current run. The scheduled run stops at the existing `maxBatches`; due-only continuations never restart repair. Reserving one slot in the final root batch guarantees repair progress even when due work fills every batch, including batch size one.

The repair UPDATE receives its page ordered by `(id, post_id)` and rechecks NULL due state and successor conditions in the writing statement. This source order is not a claim about PostgreSQL's physical row-lock order. Existing deletion checks still protect keepers, references, age and hash policy.

Repair only stamps due dates. When it stamps rows, it rewinds the due keyset through a due-only continuation so the existing source-lock protocol performs deletion, including rows whose due key sorts before the page just visited. This preserves the original lock site instead of adding a new lock use to repair.

The full local EXPLAIN harness requires `SET track_functions`, which the disposable database role cannot set. Focused plain EXPLAIN evidence is recorded above; the registered scenarios retain the existing gates for CI.

## Summary

Remove 15 explicit row locks from eight PostgreSQL trigger functions. Preserve existing validation and foreign-key checks, and validate a refund receipt against the balance returned by the lease-guarded completion write. Partition retirement now refuses immediately when a legal-hold writer conflicts with its SHARE lock. The AI usage DDL project runs its files serially and its fixture exercises the production retirement guard.

## Impact

Independent classifier, import and push-intent operations avoid redundant read locks. Refund completion returns 409 and rolls back if the saved provider amount exceeds the current balance. Partition retirement leaves the partition attached if a legal-hold writer conflicts. The backend CI shard still runs once and produces the same coverage, JUnit and profiling reports.

## Related issues

- Refs #6034 — Audits SQL functions and the two additional retirement sites; privacy/legal exceptions, unresolved concurrency sites and overlapping files remain for owner review.
Partial batch; source issue remains open for remaining work.

## Details

| --- | --- |
| Classifier threshold and result triggers locked read-only configuration for the transaction. | The triggers validate configuration without taking SHARE locks. Recorded snapshots and existing constraints preserve lineage. |
| Classifier runs and notification push intents explicitly locked referenced parents. | The existing foreign keys protect the post and conversation references. |
| New import rows took SHARE on their batch. | The trigger still checks the batch snapshot. Both import producers create the batch and every child in one transaction. |
| Refund receipt admission locked the operation before completion updated it. | Completion updates the same operation first and uses the returned balance to reject a stale receipt before persisting it. |
| Retirement could wait on a legal-hold writer after acquiring history locks. | Retirement reports existing lock contention and leaves the partition attached. |
| AI usage retirement fixtures took blocking copies of the production guard’s locks. | AI usage DDL files run serially and their fixtures exercise the production guard directly. |

Every foreign key into the retained identity and binding tables is RESTRICT and the registering function pins the identity with KEY SHARE. ## Summary

Remove redundant retention candidate prelocks while preserving guarded writes. Restore the original import cursor lock for overlapping deliveries and the hostname descendant SKIP LOCKED claim to prevent a root/child deadlock with repeated blocks. Queue ordering is not mutual exclusion.

## Impact

Cleanup keeps existing row limits, reference/hold eligibility and replay rejection behavior while holding fewer explicit locks. Restore hostname descendant and import cursor protections. The mixed operational-tombstone root and terminal Like locks remain retained for owner assessment; hostname penalty detachment still loses its redundant preclaim. The three explicitly excluded files are untouched.

## Related issues

- Refs #6034 — Retention-page audit group only; remaining moderation work and the issue's other services remain open.

## Details

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Overlapping import pages | Unlocked FK-bearing cursor can select a batch another page deletes | Restore the original FOR UPDATE on the cursor row the transaction writes |
| Vote ballot cursor read | Helper name still says lock despite an unlocked SELECT | Rename to readVoteBallotCleanupCursor and update its caller |
| Stalled job delivery | Description assumes one ordering key excludes overlap | State that a re-queued delivery can overlap the original; remove the false directive and matching registry entry |
| Other 17 removals | Existing audit removals | Keep them removed under their independent guarded-write and best-effort progress semantics |
| Hostname descendant detachment | Retention can wait on a child while holding the lifted root, against repeated blocking in the reverse order | Restore the original FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED page claim and stalled-descendant regression |

### Overlap and cursor correctness

A glide-mq ordering key or configured concurrency cap does not guarantee exclusion: a stalled job can be re-queued while its original invocation still runs. The original import cursor FOR UPDATE is restored because that same page transaction writes the cursor's FK-bearing batch position. The real-waiter regression coordinates overlapping page work and checks the resumed cursor and drained parent/child state. Removing only the restored clause produces import_retention_cursors_admin_batch_id_fkey failure 23503; restoring it passes.

The hostname descendant claim is also restored exactly as on main. Retention holds the lifted root before detaching descendants; a concurrent repeat block can hold a descendant before waiting on that root. SKIP LOCKED leaves locked descendants for a later page and avoids that deadlock. The penalty detachment preclaim remains removed because its UPDATE rechecks source_hostname_block_id. The operational-tombstone root lock remains unchanged for owner assessment; this does not exclude hostname reference cleanup from the PR.

The other reviewed removals remain. Their correctness comes from keyed conditional mutations and DELETE RETURNING, idempotent writes, and best-effort opaque progress; replay or rewind is possible under overlap. The import cursor row lock serializes same-family import page transactions. None of these conclusions relies on queue exclusion.

## Summary

Remove redundant row locks from OAuth retention, exchange recovery, claim settlement and friend-edge resolution. Repeat expiry, current state or exact ownership in guarded writes.

## Impact

Affects scheduled OAuth maintenance and provider claim admission and settlement. Batch caps and retry limits stay in place. Recovery evidence about one claim cannot settle its successor.

## Related issues

- Refs #6034 — Covers the OAuth maintenance and exchange claim portion of the row-lock audit.
Partial batch; source issue remains open for remaining work.
<!-- related-issues-validation: partial-batch -->

## Details

| Path | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OAuth request and code expiry | Prelock a bounded page before deleting it | Delete from the same bounded expiry order and check expiry in the delete |
| OAuth exchange recovery | Lock terminal and retry candidates while checking retained queue claims | Read the bounded candidate page and recheck exact claim identity when deciding recovery |
| OAuth friend edge resolution | Prelock unresolved edges after taking the target account's write lock | Conditionally update the same bounded target page |

### Concurrency

The scheduler, operator trigger, and continuation jobs share the single OAuth retention lane for request and code expiry. Exchange recovery also shares a singleton dispatcher lane. A provider worker can replace an authorization claim while recovery reads the queue. Recovery matches both the page candidate and the queue receipt to the exact authorization and claim, so evidence about the older claim cannot reject or re-enqueue a different one.

Reconnect and friend-edge cleanup write the same target account before the bounded page. The edge update also checks that the reference is still unresolved.

### Lock audit

| Class | Site | Disposition and reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| W0 | `oauth-authorization-server/retention.mts`, request/code page | Removed. A singleton sweep deletes the page under the expiry predicate. |
| W0 | `oauth/authorization-exchange-recovery-page-sql.mts`, terminal page | Removed. The terminal update checks identity, claim, state and version. |
| R | `oauth/authorization-exchange-recovery-page-sql.mts`, retry page | Removed. Re-enqueue candidates are read context. |
| W0 | `oauth-accounts/resolve-friend-reference-page.mts`, edge page | Removed. Target-account writers already own the same target row, and the conditional edge update handles contenders. |
| Q | `oauth-authorization-server/retention-tokens.mts`, child token pages | Kept for overlap with the account-lifecycle credentials worker. That worker independently selects and revokes the same token rows. |

### Exchange claim admission and settlement

Claim preparation keeps the existing writer lock for its coordinated state transitions and drops its duplicate lock on the same row. Release and exhausted rejection use conditional writes for the exact claim. Provider admission settles guarded expiry and confirms the live claim after the queue records its armed ownership. Read-only settlement outcomes can return from the current projection. Writes still recheck the exact observed claim.

| Class | Site | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| W | `oauth/authorization-exchange-state.mts`, claim preparation | Kept its existing outer lock for coordinated claim preparation and the pre-write attempt projection. |
| W0 | `oauth/authorization-exchange-state.mts`, inner claim read, release and exhausted rejection | Removed the redundant inner lock and the wrapper prelocks from guarded release and rejection. |
| R / W0 | `oauth/authorization-exchange-state.mts`, provider admission | Removed the read lock, preserving guarded expiry writes and the exact live claim check. |
| R / W0 | `oauth/authorization-exchange-disposition.mts`, missing, terminal, released and superseded reads and exact-claim settlement | Removed the blanket prelock. Settlement checks the observed claim in its writing statement. A stale claimant cannot write to its successor. |

The [first repository policy run](https://github.com/vouchington/vouchington/actions/runs/44988878705) at `8fffcc7da8` failed because the exact ordering inventory still expected the suppression removed with request and code prelocks. The original validation omitted the full repository policy scan. The owner authorized removal of that single obsolete inventory entry shared by other open PRs. ## Summary

Remove the advisory lock around follower share/send creation, keep the rolling 24-hour spam guard as a plain READ COMMITTED check, and bound route bursts with a shared per-sender Valkey rate limit.

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Two simultaneous identical sends | Advisory key makes the later request wait before checking the window | Both requests can pass the best-effort guard and commit |
| Sender scripts a burst across post and RSS share/send routes | No dedicated sender burst budget | Shared 10-request/minute budget, then 429 with `Retry-After` |
| Matching recent distribution is already visible | Existing 429 response | Same 429 response |
| Different senders share a popular post | Each takes its sender-specific advisory key | Independent ordinary transactions can both commit |

## Impact

Post and RSS-item share/send actions no longer acquire an advisory lock or use serialization conflicts for admission. The distribution and selected-recipient snapshot still commit atomically. No schema or payload changes. All four authenticated post/RSS share/send actions charge one sender-user-ID bucket before distribution work, shared across all four actions rather than keyed by IP or target post. The existing global route-rate-limit enabled switch also controls this bucket. Like the existing route mechanism, this limiter fails open on Valkey errors. The default is 10 requests per 60 seconds; DynamicConfig permits integer limits up to 100 requests and windows up to 3,600 seconds. Existing released native clients already handle the additive 429 response; no client behavior changes are needed.

## Related issues

Refs #6015 — item 2 of the advisory-lock replacements. The remaining lock sites stay in separate PRs.
<!-- related-issues-validation: partial-batch -->

## Details

### Concurrency

The rolling 24-hour guard is a best-effort spam guard, not an invariant. Two simultaneous requests with the **same sender, same action, and same post or RSS item** can both observe an empty window and insert separate distributions. This is accepted when the sender burst budget admits both requests. The route budget limits request volume; it does not make the rolling duplicate guard an invariant. No unique key, lock, claim column, or serialization conflict is added. Requests that see an existing matching distribution still receive the existing 429; failed distributions with no deliveries remain retryable under the current predicate.

| Removed site | Class | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createDistribution:lock` | R — serializes a read of the daily window | Delete the advisory query and unused key helper |

[An earlier backend run](https://github.com/vouchington/vouchington/actions/runs/44989129524) exposed conflicts between independent senders during service-backed backfill fixture creation, which the initial narrower local checks omitted. The claim retains main’s per-intake advisory before state reads and writes, including the attempt mutation’s notice/generation trigger. The transaction uses the existing READ COMMITTED behavior. Story membership changes and read-only story lookups currently share an advisory lock. Assignment and removal can update their RSS item directly and clear the former story's official item only when it still points to the moved item.

| --- | --- | --- |

Assignment and RSS refreshes use the same post-ID order for writes to existing projection jobs. A restart can wait for another transaction that changed membership. After the job write finishes, the next statement can see that transaction's committed item changes and include them in the source bound. Removal with an expected story uses a conditional write, so a stale removal leaves a recently moved item in its new story.

## Summary

Remove PostgreSQL prelocks from exact replay, pending completion, and completed authorization reads, while retaining the existing user lifecycle fence for personal credential and session writes.

## Impact

Browser and native session renewal, OAuth completion, and broker reauthentication retain their existing authority, replay, and expiry checks.

## Related issues

- Refs #6034 — Partial credential and OAuth lock-audit batch; other service sites keep the source issue open.
Partial batch; source issue remains open for remaining work.

## Details

| Path | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Device renewal | Prelock the user and session before checking for exact replay | Return an eligible persisted replay from a primary read. Intended writes retain the existing user privacy fence and check current session authority in the update. |
| OAuth completion | Prelock the actor and authorization for pending, replay and write branches | Authenticate the proof from the current projection and reserve the existing writer locks for live, ready completion. Check actor eligibility from primary reads for pending and replay. |
| Broker reauthentication | Prelock the completed authorization before consuming a separate verified challenge | Read the exact completed authorization and keep the existing active session and one-shot challenge checks. |

### Concurrency

A rotation writes only while the presented digest, session identity, detailed authority and device binding still match. A losing browser rotation can return the exact committed credential only while its predecessor is in grace and the proof-authorized binding stays the same. A committed revocation rejects the stale rotation. A committed registration requires fresh proof and cannot be overwritten by an earlier unbound request.

A completed OAuth replay validates its own caller and proof. A request that loses writable admission rereads current proof and readiness before returning a stored result. A ready completion retains the lock while applying its ordered account, authorization and session effects. Broker challenge consumption is independent of the completion acknowledgement token.

### Lock audit

| Class | Site | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R | `jwt-session/device-authority-rotation.mts`, exact replay | Removed the session row prelock. A pure replay reads the exact persisted credential and current active authority. |
| W0 | `jwt-session/device-authority-rotation.mts`, rotation, reuse revocation and replay registration | Removed the session row prelock. Each write checks the authority it depends on. |
| P | `jwt-session/device-authority-rotation.mts`, users-row writer admission | Kept for personal session writes and the existing user-before-session deletion order. An admitted writer can lose its conditional update and resolve as replay. |
| W0 | `mfa/active-account-session.mts`, duplicate users-row SHARE | Removed. The same transaction already acquired the existing exclusive user lifecycle fence. |
| R | `oauth/authorization-completion-transaction.mts`, pending and exact result replay | Removed the authorization and actor row prelocks from read-only admission. |
| W0 | `oauth/authorization-completion-transaction.mts`, expiry cleanup | Removed the blanket prelock. Expiry cleanup tests the deadline and protects completed results in the update. |
| P / W | `oauth/authorization-completion-transaction.mts`, ready completion | Kept the user privacy fence and narrowed the authorization lock to the live ready row this transaction completes. |
| R | `oauth/provider-reauth-broker.mts`, completed authorization read | Removed the authorization row prelock, preserving the active-account session fence for the durable proof write. |

### CI findings

Run `44996122339` exposed the changed session authority file’s complexity score of 54 against the repository cap of 50. A fixed list of authority fields now expresses the same strict comparisons directly.

Run `44997041307` found duplicate reads of current session authority. A live rotation now uses one primary authority read and checks that exact authority in the conditional write. A losing write continues to reread the current persisted outcome.

Run `44998396487` reported backend patch coverage at 94 of 101 lines. The earlier local suite did not reach seven defensive and concurrent states, including a browser or native rotation losing to a committed winner and an active SID without durable device authority. The focused coverage report now shows hits on all seven lines, and the regressions check the returned outcome and persisted credential or session state.


### Session refresh race outcomes

| Scenario | Before review correction | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The presented device digest is still current but a concurrent replay registration changed its binding | Lost rotation returned `SESSION_RELOGIN_REQUIRED`. | Return `DBSC_PROOF_REQUIRED` (403), preserving the winning digest and binding. |
| Replay registration loses its conditional write to a further device rotation | The stale replay could return without revoking the current session. | Reread authoritative state and apply the existing credential-reuse revocation to the latest session; return `SESSION_REFRESH_REUSED` (401). |

These are the existing main security outcomes. Both paths use the persisted current authority and existing guarded writes. No lock, retry, or coordination field is added.

body:
## Summary

Email login and re-auth code requests now have a minimum interval (default 60 s, DynamicConfig `email-auth-limits-config.code_request_min_interval_seconds`, 0 to 3600, 0 disables). A request inside the interval gets the existing 429 with a `Retry-After` header (the api-client turns it into `retry_after`) before any code is created or email enqueued. Success responses carry `resend_after_seconds`, and web disables resend with a countdown, guards double submits, and routes resend and re-auth send errors through `onError`.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Server spacing | 5 requests per 60 s per email, IP, device and session; no minimum gap, each new code invalidates the last | Same 5-per-60 s limits, plus one code per normalized email (login) or per session (re-auth) per interval; refusal is 429 with `Retry-After` |
| Refused request | n/a | Charges nothing (`RateLimiter.consume`), so the interval runs from the last admitted send and is never extended by retries |
| Success response | `{ email_address }` | `{ email_address, resend_after_seconds }` (fixtures marked `pending` for native adoption) |
| Web login email submit | No in-flight guard; two clicks in one tick both submit | Ref guard; submits once |
| Web resend (login, re-auth) | Enabled whenever not loading; resend errors showed raw API text | Disabled with a `Resend in Ns` countdown from `resend_after_seconds` or `retry_after`; errors go through `onError` shared 429 handling |
| Re-auth resend on 429 | Cleared the code pane before sending, dropping the user to the send pane | Keeps the code pane; countdown starts from `retry_after` |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  R[Code request] --> A[5-per-60s limits]
  A -->|limited| X[429]
  A --> I{Interval slot free?}
  I -->|no| T[429 + Retry-After, nothing recorded]
  I -->|yes| C[Create code, enqueue email]
  C --> S[200 with resend_after_seconds]
```

## Impact

Web users see a resend countdown and a single submit. Released native clients are unaffected: the 429 with `Retry-After` is already handled, and the new response field is additive (fixtures `pending`, parity matrix row added with Swift and .NET marked pending client adoption). Test baseline sets the interval to 0 so existing suites that send several codes to one email or session are unaffected. A slot is spent when admitted, so a failure after admission (for example a 422 disposable domain) still makes the user wait one interval.

## Related issues

- Closes #6126 — Implements the issue

## Details

Limiter: `RateLimiter.consume` with threshold 2 and cost 1 in `backend/services/users/email-auth-rate-limits.mts`; runs after the unchanged 5-per-60 s `addAndCheck` and before code creation.

429 header: `app.errorHandler` sets `Retry-After` from `retryAfterSeconds` on a 429 error; no body field was added because the api-client derives `retry_after` from the header.

Success interval comes from the response (`resend_after_seconds`) rather than a public config fetch: it is exact per send, needs no extra request, and the web has no DynamicConfig-backed public config pattern for this.

Catalog: `extracted.emailCodeResend.resendIn` added with `pnpm run localization:catalog` in en-US, es, fr, pt; `routes.json` and `route-selectors.generated.mts` regenerated.

Fixtures regenerated with `pnpm run api-fixtures:generate` after updating the explicit response contracts in `api-fixtures/v1/manifest.json`.

Not run locally: the worktree is not initialized, so vitest and DB-backed tests ran only in CI. Run locally: backend and web `tsc`, oxlint, oxfmt, `api-fixtures:check`, route-selector `--check`, live route localization check.

body:
## Problem

When PostgreSQL uses a generic plan to look up a current provider membership binding, it cannot infer the partial-index predicates from the bound source kind. The lookup can visit every retained binding on that lineage before finding the single current row.

## Change

Use literal direct and family predicates so PostgreSQL can select the existing partial unique indexes. Direct still looks up the current lineage owner and checks it against the requesting account. Family still looks up the current binding for the requested user. Both require an unreleased binding and run after the existing conflict-tolerant insert in the same transaction.

## Before and after

The captures use SQL extracted from the baseline and final service, 110,100 released bindings and 2,142 current bindings across 102 synthetic lineages in a rolled-back PostgreSQL transaction. JIT was off and work_mem was 32 MB. Every measured lookup returned one row.

| Forced plan and target history | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Generic, 10,000 released bindings | Lineage index scans 10,021 rows and filters 10,020, 264 shared hits for either kind | Current partial unique index reads one row, 2 shared hits for direct and 3 for family |
| Generic, 100 released bindings | Lineage index scans 121 rows and filters 120, 9 shared hits for either kind | Current partial unique index reads one row, 2 shared hits for direct and 3 for family |
| Custom, either history size | Current partial unique index reads one row, 2 shared hits for direct and 3 for family | Same indexes and work |

Full result sets matched for same-account direct, other-account direct, existing family, missing family user, and missing lineage. Removing the family user filter in the control matched 20 current rows instead of one.

Refs #5745

## Upstream repros

With `no-mistakes 0.109.109`, `postgres-bounded-statements` reports the nested CTID-array predicate as an unbounded UPDATE. In the same synthetic catalog it accepts a direct CTID array and complete composite primary-key equality; the unrestricted UPDATE control is correctly reported too. Its CTID input separately comes from an exact-pair lock query over a page capped at hard max 1000; this repro makes no claim about cross-statement flow.

```sql

  id uuid NOT NULL,
  group_id uuid NOT NULL,
  payload text NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (id, group_id)
);
```

reason: Pilot verdict at this head found 3 real defect(s), first: new web on an old backend: undefined total_is_exact and next_cursor make every viewer get the section with a Keep looking that refetches the same page; the author fixed it in a later head. The full review run at this head reported 1 of the 3 expected findings.

expected.claim: Backend and web deploy separately, so the web can run against a backend that does not return total_is_exact or next_cursor. The section then treats undefined as not exact and not null and shows Keep looking forever. Treat total_is_exact !== false as exact and use next_cursor ?? null.
The requirements doc says social proof modules short-circuit to null when all totals are zero, but the change now renders the card for inexact zero totals. Update the doc line.

body:
The topic follower preview now starts with people the viewer followed most recently. This can change which five people appear. Previously it started with people who followed that topic most recently.

## Topic follower context

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First request | Count every eligible topic follower and preview five in topic-follow order | Inspect a bounded viewer-follow window, return up to five eligible people in viewer-follow order, and say whether the count is exact |
| Viewer follows more eligible people than the preview can hold | No continuation | Continue from the last returned user's viewer-follow edge |
| All inspected users are ineligible | Compute the exact count | Return an empty page with a continuation if the viewer has more own follows to inspect |
| A private or unfollowed account follows or unfollows the topic | The viewer sees no change | The viewer sees no change to the results, count, exactness, or continuation |

The topic follower group keeps `total: number` and `users: PublicUser[]`. It adds `total_is_exact: boolean` and `next_cursor: string | null`. Optional `after` resumes that group and the count then describes the inspected suffix. Page counts describe overlapping suffixes and should never be added together. The vote groups retain their existing format. The JSON change is additive. The current clients-main common decoders tolerate unknown fields; no topic follow-context consumer was found there. No released binary was verified. Richer presentation and continuation are pending. [Native adoption](https://github.com/vouchington/vouchington-clients/issues/758)

The existing users work configuration sets the reported-count default and ceiling to 99 and the inspected viewer-follow default and ceiling to 1,000. SQL binds both inspection values and reserves one lookahead. A count below the preview size also limits the number of returned users. The encrypted cursor preserves microseconds and authenticates its viewer and topic scope.

## PostgreSQL evidence

The same PostgreSQL fixture has 50,000 active outgoing follows for the viewer. That is the documented hard maximum for `relation-limits-config.follow_user`, whose default is 10,000. The fixture has 50,000 topic follows and 30,000 unrelated newer follows spread across distinct timestamps. Prepared captures used JIT off and 32 MB `work_mem`. The table shows one local sample per mode from the rolled-back fixture. These local captures are separate from the existing hosted small-scenario gate, which keeps its current budgets.

| Query | Custom | Generic |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original exact count | Scans 87,142 user-follow rows on the driving scan, 50,000 topic follows, 24.599 ms | Reads 50,000 outgoing follows and runs 10,000 keyed topic probes, 58.965 ms |
| Viewer-driven first page | One index search reads 1,001 outgoing follows, 5.265 ms | One index search reads 1,001 outgoing follows, 4.013 ms |
| Viewer-driven continuation after outgoing edge 45,001 | One index search reads 1,001 outgoing follows, 1.373 ms | One index search reads 1,001 outgoing follows, 1.330 ms |

Both final shapes use the existing `idx_relation__user__follow__user__subject__newest` order index at the hard maximum. The continuation has the full timestamp/user tuple in the index condition. Viewer-edge selection precedes eligibility. The eligibility checks use the account primary key and keyed topic and reciprocal follow indexes. There is no index migration. The same fixture's one-follow viewer reads one outgoing row in each mode.

With the viewer graph held fixed, inserting and removing a private topic follow and 1,400 unfollowed topic edges left the viewer-driven query rows byte-identical in a separate paired check. One viewer retained an exact total of six and the same continuation position. A second viewer retained an exact total of three and no continuation. The public response tests exercise both empty continuation and complete-page cases through the same topic endpoint.

## Bounded-statement advisory

With pinned no-mistakes 0.109.111 and the same 180/55 budgets, replacing only this query with its main version reports one finding at this site; the final query reports zero. The paired whole-tree bounded-statement counts are 82 → 81, and non-copyright counts are 46 → 45. Both checks exit successfully because this rule is advisory.

## Web and native adoption

Web renders non-exact counts through the translation catalog and lets the viewer explicitly continue an incomplete preview until five distinct people appear or the cursor ends. Empty incomplete pages remain visible, and failed requests retain their cursor for retry. Page suffix counts are combined conservatively, never summed. The parity matrix records the pending Swift and .NET work in [clients #758](https://github.com/vouchington/vouchington-clients/issues/758).

No schema, index, lock, dependency, or persistence changes are required.

## Local validation gaps caught by CI

[Static run 45028191866](https://github.com/vouchington/vouchington/actions/runs/45028191866) at `1afce2df641077bd1db9d60ebfc9c4c94d0c6f26` caught missing direct Storybook coverage for the newly exported `FollowContextUserList`. Local focused browser stories rendered the enclosing section, and the full component-story inventory was omitted. A dedicated runtime-import story now passes that exact inventory and the four focused Chromium stories. The coverage gate and exclusions are unchanged.

[Web run 45028705040](https://github.com/vouchington/vouchington/actions/runs/45028705040) at `25cbd2a34daf19c0943d58fb4f7bf3ade870c420` then caught the new HTTP helper's uncovered line. Component tests mocked this boundary, and changed-line API coverage had not been checked locally. A transport-level test now executes the actual helper, verifies encoded opaque cursors and returned metadata, and passes the unchanged web API patch-coverage rule at 100%.

Refs #5745

title: refactor(data-retention): remove redundant cleanup page locks
reason: Pilot final verdict APPROVE with no defect findings: removes redundant retention page locks and restores the claims that guard something; the final verdict approved with no defect findings.
body:
## Summary

Remove redundant retention prelocks while retaining main's protections for overlapping import purges, retained-reference writers, hostname detach work, ballot cursor progression, flag redaction and legal-record references. Restore the original claims required by the per-site concurrency review.

## Impact

Cleanup keeps its existing caps, reference/hold eligibility and replay rules. Busy retained roots and detach rows are skipped while unrelated work progresses. The mixed operational-tombstone root and terminal Like locks remain retained for owner assessment; the three excluded files are untouched.

## Related issues

- Refs #6034 — Retention-page audit batch only; other services and retained owner-decision sites remain outside this PR.
Partial batch; source issue remains open for remaining work.
<!-- related-issues-validation: partial-batch -->

## Details

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Overlapping import cursor writes | Unlocked FK-bearing cursor can checkpoint a deleted batch | Keep the original cursor FOR UPDATE |
| Import parent purges | Child pages read an unclaimed parent | Restore main's active-parent FOR UPDATE and next-parent SKIP LOCKED selection |
| Retained roots and media references | A stale anti-join can wait or fail at a restrictive FK | Restore root/binding claims and the image read-context claim; reclaim unrelated unlocked orphans |
| Hostname reblock and admin purge | Descendant or penalty detachment can wait in an opposing lock order | Restore both main SKIP LOCKED pages; keep the penalty's source recheck |
| Unscoped ballot sweeps | Overlapping pages can reach the checkpoint after touching ballots | Restore cursor FOR UPDATE before selection; explicit ID-scoped calls retain main's bypass |
| Queue scheduling | Ordering was treated as exclusion | State that stalled deliveries overlap; keep the false directive and registry entry removed |
| Vote-integrity detail redaction | Direct updates can wait behind parent/merge/resolver writers in another row order | Restore main's ordered materialized flag claim and SKIP LOCKED |
| Legal entitlement attempts | An uncommitted child is absent from the anti-join but pins its grant parent | Restore source SKIP LOCKED so unrelated expired attempts progress without a RESTRICT failure |
| Other audit removals | Redundant prelocks | Keep the remaining guarded-write and best-effort checkpoint removals |

### Overlap and progress

A glide-mq ordering key or concurrency cap does not guarantee exclusion: a stalled delivery can overlap its original invocation. The original import cursor lock is retained because the transaction writes an FK-bearing position. The original parent clauses arbitrate with purges before child reads; new-parent selection skips busy parents. Child/lookahead claim removals remain.

Retained identity and binding claims cover rows the transaction deletes. Concurrent children hold FK KEY SHARE and RESTRICT alone can make a stale anti-join delete wait or fail, rolling back unrelated page progress. The image claim is read context, restored exactly as main by explicit user direction. The original live-placement/pinned-identity regression and helper are restored.

Hostname descendants and penalties retain main's SKIP LOCKED claims; their source rechecks remain. The original unscoped ballot cursor lock is acquired before ballot reads/mutations and is named lockVoteBallotCleanupCursor again. Explicit voteIds calls bypass that cursor as on main; no new scoped lock use is added.

Vote-integrity redaction again claims selected flag IDs with main's ordered materialized SKIP LOCKED CTE, then updates FROM locked. This avoids waiting on flags held by a post cascade, relation merge or resolver-user SET NULL. The flag checkpoint prelock remains removed. Legal record selection restores FOR UPDATE OF source SKIP LOCKED; the entitlement self-reference is RESTRICT, and a concurrent child holds KEY SHARE before the anti-join can see it. The observed missing-claim control raises PostgreSQL 23001 (restrict_violation).

These are main restorations, not new lock sites. The remaining removals rely on conditional writes, DELETE RETURNING, reference constraints and best-effort opaque progress. The false vote-ballot scheduling directive and its ordering-policy entry stay removed. No table, column, retry, cap or schedule change is introduced.

### Lock classification

<details>
<summary>Every assigned site, including retained and restored locks</summary>

| Base file and line | Class | Disposition and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cleanup-activitypub-replay.mts:61 | W0 | Remove floor prelock. Only daily cleanup writes production floor; inbox admission reads that floor in the conditional INSERT without a lock. The floor UPDATE is monotone and commits with the DELETE. |
| cleanup-activitypub-replay.mts:69 | W0 | Remove prelock. Inbox source is insert-only outside this sweep, which is reached only from daily federation cleanup. The actual DELETE already matches bounded IDs and the age bound. |
| cleanup-activitypub-tombstones.mts:47 | Q (Follow) / ? (Like) | Keep pending owner decision for Like. Daily and dedicated family workers overlap. Follow deletes the selected terminal identities. Like may preserve a selected identity when it has a live payload. Removing the Like prelock reverses lock order against ingress: a freshly signed Undo can name an old Like, update its terminal identity through ON CONFLICT, and then wait for the payload held by cleanup. Cleanup in turn waits to delete the identity held by Undo. The guarded DELETE and RESTRICT FK protect referenced identities, but the interleaving can still deadlock the cleanup page. |
| cleanup-deferred-post-votes.mts:53 | W | Keep. Separate due selection, superseded ballot DELETE/tally and current-ballot marker clear must coordinate with ordinary post-vote updates and outbound distribution. Writes consume the selected due source state. |
| cleanup-federation-candidates.mts:16 | W0 | Remove. Only daily follower sweep selects this family. Follower processor writes only active deliveries and DELETE rechecks terminal state. |
| cleanup-federation-delete.mts:20 | W0 | Remove. Bounded same-statement DELETE rechecks terminal state on its target. |
| cleanup-federation-purge-identities.mts:14 | W0 | Remove. Same-statement bounded UPDATE rechecks target and active status. Concurrent Undo cannot be overwritten. |
| cleanup-hacker-news.mts:59 | W | Keep. The totals row is deleted in the transaction after stories and comments. Refresh obtains the same totals lock before replacing children; selector carries the prior presence fact for the after-commit flag job. |
| cleanup-hostname-block-references.mts:36 | Q | Restored original FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. The transaction detaches these descendants while holding their lifted root. Skip a descendant held by a repeated block that may itself wait on that root; remaining references report stalled progress and are retried on a later page. |
| cleanup-hostname-block-references.mts:51 | Q | Restore main penalty SKIP LOCKED claim on rows detached in this transaction. Preserve the UPDATE source_hostname_block_id recheck; skip dependents held by competing admin/purge work. |
| cleanup-import-batches.mts:64 | W | Restored original FOR UPDATE. The page transaction writes this FK-bearing cursor; overlapping deliveries otherwise can checkpoint a deleted batch and fail with 23503. Real-waiter clause-removal regression reproduces that error. |
| cleanup-import-batches.mts:75 | R / W | Restore main FOR UPDATE per user. This is read context on child-only pages and a written parent on final deletion; acquire it before reading children to arbitrate the selected page with purge. |
| cleanup-import-batches.mts:86 | R / Q | Restore main FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED per user. A claimed parent is read context on child-only pages; terminal paths write/delete it. Skip a pinned candidate so another completed batch can progress. |
| cleanup-import-batches.mts:108 | W0 | Remove child prelock. Bounded DELETE rechecks immutable composite discovery identity and batch; the read also includes an unwritten lookahead. |
| cleanup-import-batches.mts:142 | W0 | Remove child prelock. Bounded DELETE rechecks ID and batch on finalized imports and leaves the lookahead untouched. |
| cleanup-legal-records.mts:109 | Q / R | Restore main FOR UPDATE OF source SKIP LOCKED. Claim rows then deleted; the preserved pageSize+1 lookahead is read context. An uncommitted entitlement child holds FK KEY SHARE and the grant_entitlement_attempt_id self-reference is RESTRICT, so the stale anti-join must skip rather than fail the page. |
| cleanup-operational-tombstone-candidates.mts:33 | Q / ? | Keep. Daily and per-family jobs overlap. The ordinary path deletes selected tombstones. Hostname cleanup can instead detach dependents or advance past a protected source, leaving that source untouched in that transaction. Audit question is whether the existing source lock should be removed specifically for that path given the overlapping hostname writers and existing per-family cursor lock. |
| cleanup-operational-tombstones.mts:84 | W | Keep. Daily and per-family processors can checkpoint the same cursor. Serializes stale cursor advancement and resumption, including partial hostname child draining. |
| cleanup-retained-identities.mts:52 | W0 | Keep removed. Cursor writes are opaque best-effort progress and may replay under overlap; scoped callers bypass the cursor and guarded DELETE keeps live-reference checks. |
| cleanup-retained-identities.mts:86 | Q | Restore main locked candidate CTE and SKIP LOCKED on the delete targets. Preserve anti-reference guards; a child FK KEY SHARE/RESTRICT race must not roll back the whole page. |
| cleanup-retained-media-bindings.mts:66 | W0 | Keep removed. Cursor writes are best-effort progress; source DELETE keeps current live/durable reference guards. Overlap is permitted. |
| cleanup-retained-media-bindings.mts:92 | R | Restore main lockRetainedMediaBindingImages by explicit user direction. This read-context image claim preserves bindings for pinned roots while unrelated orphans progress. |
| cleanup-retained-media-bindings.mts:99 | Q | Restore main lockRetainedMediaBindings on the bindings then deleted. Keep the corresponding reference guards and SKIP LOCKED behavior. |
| cleanup-vote-ballot-cursor.mts:25 | W | Restore main cursor FOR UPDATE and truthful lockVoteBallotCleanupCursor name. Unscoped sweeps lock their checkpoint before reading/mutating ballots; explicit ID-scoped calls retain main's bypass. |
| cleanup-vote-ballots.mts:148 | W0 (mutation page) / R (one lookahead) | Keep removed. DELETE rechecks an immutable same-entity newer ballot and tallies only DELETE RETURNING rows, so duplicate candidates cannot be tallied twice. Deferred markers are best-effort progress; the extra lookahead is never written. Stalled invocations can overlap. |
| cleanup-vote-integrity-details.mts:42 | W0 | Keep removed. The checkpoint is best-effort progress and can be replayed by overlapping deliveries; targeted calls bypass it. Correctness comes from the keyed writing statement, not queue exclusion. |
| cleanup-vote-integrity-details.mts:74 | Q | Restore main WITH locked AS MATERIALIZED, ordered by immutable id, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and UPDATE FROM locked. These flag rows are redacted in this transaction; skip rows held by parent deletion, topic merge or resolved_by_id SET NULL writers. |

The text matches in cleanup-operational-tombstone-candidates.mts:24 and security-record-plans.mts:84 are comments. The latter describes the separately excluded security-record-page.mts. Also excluded are abandoned-bluesky-sessions.mts and cleanup-retained-relation-identities.mts from #6020. No P sites in this group on this base. The terminal Like and mixed operational tombstone candidate sites need the owner's decision.


</details>

### EXPLAIN validation

The scoped, global and continuation scenarios gate the actual bounded candidate SELECT with the existing accepted indexes and 25-row budget. The guarded DELETE has only local raw-plan verification; it is not claimed to be covered by the real-row gate.

The retained-media scenario again captures all three original statements: candidate read, image claim and binding claim. The scoped retention scenario passed in custom and generic modes on both capture passes with its existing budgets. A private Unix-socket PostgreSQL copy of only the disposable worktree database supplied local function counters without modifying shared roles. The neighboring staging scenario was not fully seeded by this scoped run, so this is not a claim of full-shard success.

### CI verification gap

[Backend EXPLAIN run 44991317199](https://github.com/vouchington/vouchington/actions/runs/44991317199) at `3256fe9c195a6efafb55764e38607dd7242f3c81` rejected the scoped capture: a DELETE without RETURNING reports zero root rows, so it cannot satisfy the existing real-row admission assertion. Before that push, the disposable database role could not enable `track_functions`; fallback validation replayed raw EXPLAIN but omitted that admission assertion.

The correction captures the surviving bounded candidate SELECT, matching the global and continuation scenarios. The actual admission/index/row checks were then run against the captured plans in both forced modes: the candidate passes and the former DELETE capture reproduces the CI rejection. No production output, empty-plan exception, row budget or accepted-index relaxation was added. The full registered scenario remains enforced by CI.

### Existing import-order limitation

A separate synthetic admin-parent purge can still invert main's active cursor and parent locks when the purge acquires the parent first and its SET NULL action waits for the cursor. That 40P01 is present with the restored main clauses; this PR does not claim to eliminate every import deadlock. The production RSS cascade follows an analogous source-level order, but that path has not been reproduced and is not presented as a confirmed production incident.

### Remaining waits and repeated work

- Federation: ordinary guarded UPDATE/DELETE operations can wait on concurrent writers and revisit selected terminal rows.
- Replay ledger: expired-row deletion and the monotonic freshness-floor update can wait or repeat work during overlapping cleanup. They still commit in the same transaction.
- Import child pages, including RSS discoveries: DELETE acquires its ordinary row locks and can wait. Import child deletes no longer have a guaranteed id order; ORDER BY in candidate selection does not guarantee DELETE execution or lock order.
- Retained identity/media cursors: pages can overlap or revisit bounded ranges, and checkpoint UPDATE itself can wait after page work has happened.
- Older ballots: guarded UPDATE/DELETE can wait or repeat selected history behind other mutations, even though unscoped sweeps acquire their cursor first.

These remaining removals retain blocking DML rather than main's separate skip/claim behavior. This is best-effort progress, not single-flight or general deadlock freedom; a skipped row can require a later fresh sweep rather than the current continuation.

title: fix(follower-distributions): remove advisory locks and rate-limit senders
reason: Pilot final verdict APPROVE with no defect findings: removes the follower-distribution advisory lock and adds a per-sender budget; the final verdict approved with only nits after the MCP-budget fix.
body:
## Summary

Remove the advisory lock around follower share/send creation, keep the rolling 24-hour spam guard as a plain READ COMMITTED check, and bound REST and MCP share/send bursts with one shared per-sender Valkey rate limit.

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Two simultaneous identical sends | Advisory key makes the later request wait before checking the window | Both requests can pass the best-effort guard and commit |
| Sender scripts a burst across REST and MCP post/RSS share/send actions | General per-route limits; no shared sender budget | Shared 10-request/minute budget; REST 429 with `Retry-After` and MCP typed rate-limit result with retry seconds |
| Matching recent distribution is already visible | Existing 429 response | Same 429 response |
| Different senders share a popular post | Each takes its sender-specific advisory key | Independent ordinary transactions can both commit |

## Impact

Post and RSS-item share/send actions no longer acquire an advisory lock or use serialization conflicts for admission. The distribution and selected-recipient snapshot still commit atomically. No schema or payload changes. All four post/RSS share/send service operations charge one sender-user-ID bucket exactly once, before opening their distribution transaction. REST and MCP calls share this budget across all four actions rather than splitting it by transport, IP, or target. Existing general REST per-route limits remain in place. The existing global route-rate-limit enabled switch also controls this bucket. REST retains `Retry-After` through the shared service error metadata; MCP uses its existing typed `RATE_LIMIT` result and `retryAfterSeconds`. Like the existing route mechanism, this limiter fails open on Valkey errors. The default is 10 requests per 60 seconds; DynamicConfig permits integer limits up to 100 requests and windows up to 3,600 seconds.
