title: Bound topic follower context by viewer follow recency
reason: Pilot final verdict APPROVE with no defect findings: bounded topic follow-context walk with an encrypted cursor; the final verdict approved after the three nits were fixed.
body:
The topic follower preview now starts with people the viewer followed most recently. This can change which five people appear. Previously it started with people who followed that topic most recently.

## Topic follower context

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First request | Count every eligible topic follower and preview five in topic-follow order | Inspect a bounded viewer-follow window, return up to five eligible people in viewer-follow order, and say whether the count is exact |
| Viewer follows more eligible people than the preview can hold | No continuation | Continue from the last returned user's viewer-follow edge |
| All inspected users are ineligible | Compute the exact count | Return an empty page with a continuation if the viewer has more own follows to inspect |
| A private or unfollowed account follows or unfollows the topic | The viewer sees no change | The viewer sees no change to the results, count, exactness, or continuation |

The topic follower group keeps `total: number` and `users: PublicUser[]`. It adds `total_is_exact: boolean` and `next_cursor: string | null`. Optional `after` resumes that group and the count then describes the inspected suffix. Page counts describe overlapping suffixes and should never be added together. The vote groups retain their existing format. The JSON change is additive. The current clients-main common decoders tolerate unknown fields; no topic follow-context consumer was found there. No released binary was verified. Richer presentation and continuation are pending. [Native adoption](https://github.com/vouchington/vouchington-clients/issues/758)

The existing users work configuration sets the reported-count default and ceiling to 99 and the inspected viewer-follow default and ceiling to 1,000. SQL binds both inspection values and reserves one lookahead. A count below the preview size also limits the number of returned users. The encrypted cursor preserves microseconds and authenticates its viewer and topic scope.

Web also accepts backend responses without the new metadata: it renders the legacy exact count and treats a missing cursor as exhausted. Initial requests retain both vote groups. Follower continuations skip their vote lookups and hydration, returning the existing vote-group fields empty; web retains the initial vote context.

## PostgreSQL evidence

The same PostgreSQL fixture has 50,000 active outgoing follows for the viewer. That is the documented hard maximum for `relation-limits-config.follow_user`, whose default is 10,000. The fixture has 50,000 topic follows and 30,000 unrelated newer follows spread across distinct timestamps. Prepared captures used JIT off and 32 MB `work_mem`. The table shows one local sample per mode from the rolled-back fixture. These local captures are separate from the existing hosted small-scenario gate, which keeps its current budgets.

| Query | Custom | Generic |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original exact count | Scans 87,142 user-follow rows on the driving scan, 50,000 topic follows, 24.599 ms | Reads 50,000 outgoing follows and runs 10,000 keyed topic probes, 58.965 ms |
| Viewer-driven first page | One index search reads 1,001 outgoing follows, 5.265 ms | One index search reads 1,001 outgoing follows, 4.013 ms |
| Viewer-driven continuation after outgoing edge 45,001 | One index search reads 1,001 outgoing follows, 1.373 ms | One index search reads 1,001 outgoing follows, 1.330 ms |

Both final shapes use the existing `idx_relation__user__follow__user__subject__newest` order index at the hard maximum. The continuation has the full timestamp/user tuple in the index condition. Viewer-edge selection precedes eligibility. The eligibility checks use the account primary key and keyed topic and reciprocal follow indexes. There is no index migration. The same fixture's one-follow viewer reads one outgoing row in each mode.

With the viewer graph held fixed, inserting and removing a private topic follow and 1,400 unfollowed topic edges left the viewer-driven query rows byte-identical in a separate paired check. One viewer retained an exact total of six and the same continuation position. A second viewer retained an exact total of three and no continuation. The public response tests exercise both empty continuation and complete-page cases through the same topic endpoint.

## Bounded-statement advisory

With pinned no-mistakes 0.109.111 and the same 180/55 budgets, replacing only this query with its main version reports one finding at this site; the final query reports zero. The paired whole-tree bounded-statement counts are 82 → 81, and non-copyright counts are 46 → 45. Both checks exit successfully because this rule is advisory.

## Web and native adoption

Web renders non-exact counts through the translation catalog and lets the viewer explicitly continue an incomplete preview until five distinct people appear or the cursor ends. Empty incomplete pages remain visible, and failed requests retain their cursor for retry. Page suffix counts are combined conservatively, never summed. The parity matrix records the pending Swift and .NET work in [clients #758](https://github.com/vouchington/vouchington-clients/issues/758).

No schema, index, lock, dependency, or persistence changes are required.

## Local validation gaps caught by CI

[Static run 45028191866](https://github.com/vouchington/vouchington/actions/runs/45028191866) at `1afce2df641077bd1db9d60ebfc9c4c94d0c6f26` caught missing direct Storybook coverage for the newly exported `FollowContextUserList`. Local focused browser stories rendered the enclosing section, and the full component-story inventory was omitted. A dedicated runtime-import story now passes that exact inventory and the four focused Chromium stories. The coverage gate and exclusions are unchanged.

[Web run 45028705040](https://github.com/vouchington/vouchington/actions/runs/45028705040) at `25cbd2a34daf19c0943d58fb4f7bf3ade870c420` then caught the new HTTP helper's uncovered line. The lower also restores conditional predecessor wakes on insertion and deleted-to-live restoration, including committed check_newest work. It uses a fresh keeper-check phase before settlement; reconciliation does not rewrite plain-due rows. Settled keepers leave the work index. reason: Pilot final verdict APPROVE with no defect findings: removes OAuth and friend-edge row locks after the FOR NO KEY UPDATE SKIP LOCKED fix; approved with no findings.
body:
## Summary

Remove redundant row locks from OAuth retention, exchange recovery, claim settlement and friend-edge resolution. Repeat expiry, current state or exact ownership in guarded writes.

## Impact

Affects scheduled OAuth maintenance and provider claim admission and settlement. Batch caps and retry limits stay in place. Recovery evidence about one claim cannot settle its successor.

## Related issues

- Refs #6034 — Partial OAuth maintenance and exchange claim lock-audit batch; other service sites keep the source issue open.
Partial batch; source issue remains open for remaining work.
<!-- related-issues-validation: partial-batch -->

## Details

| Path | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OAuth request and code expiry | Prelock a bounded page before deleting it | Delete from the same bounded expiry order and check expiry in the delete |
| OAuth exchange recovery | Lock terminal and retry candidates while checking retained queue claims | Read the bounded candidate page and recheck exact claim identity when deciding recovery |
| OAuth friend edge resolution | Prelock unresolved edges after taking the target account's write lock | Conditionally update the same bounded target page |

### Concurrency

The scheduler, operator trigger, and continuation jobs share the single OAuth retention lane for request and code expiry. Exchange recovery also shares a singleton dispatcher lane. A provider worker can replace an authorization claim while recovery reads the queue. Recovery matches both the page candidate and the queue receipt to the exact authorization and claim, so evidence about the older claim cannot reject or re-enqueue a different one.

Reconnect and friend-edge cleanup write the same target account before the bounded page. The edge update also checks that the reference is still unresolved.

### Lock audit

| Class | Site | Disposition and reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| W0 | `oauth-authorization-server/retention.mts`, request/code page | Removed. A singleton sweep deletes the page under the expiry predicate. |
| W0 | `oauth/authorization-exchange-recovery-page-sql.mts`, terminal page | Removed. The terminal update checks identity, claim, state and version. |
| R | `oauth/authorization-exchange-recovery-page-sql.mts`, retry page | Removed. Re-enqueue candidates are read context. |
| W0 | `oauth-accounts/resolve-friend-reference-page.mts`, edge page | Removed. Target-account writers already own the same target row, and the conditional edge update handles contenders. |
| Q | `oauth-authorization-server/retention-tokens.mts`, child token pages | Kept for overlap with the account-lifecycle credentials worker. That worker independently selects and revokes the same token rows. |

### Exchange claim admission and settlement

Claim preparation keeps the existing writer lock for its coordinated state transitions and drops its duplicate lock on the same row. Release and exhausted rejection use conditional writes for the exact claim. Provider admission settles guarded expiry and confirms the live claim after the queue records its armed ownership. Read-only settlement outcomes can return from the current projection. Writes still recheck the exact observed claim.

| Class | Site | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| W | `oauth/authorization-exchange-state.mts`, claim preparation | Kept its existing outer lock for coordinated claim preparation and the pre-write attempt projection. |
| W0 | `oauth/authorization-exchange-state.mts`, inner claim read, release and exhausted rejection | Removed the redundant inner lock and the wrapper prelocks from guarded release and rejection. |
| R / W0 | `oauth/authorization-exchange-state.mts`, provider admission | Removed the read lock, preserving guarded expiry writes and the exact live claim check. |
| R / W0 | `oauth/authorization-exchange-disposition.mts`, missing, terminal, released and superseded reads and exact-claim settlement | Removed the blanket prelock. Settlement checks the observed claim in its writing statement. A stale claimant cannot write to its successor. |

### CI diagnosis

The [first repository policy run](https://github.com/vouchington/vouchington/actions/runs/44988878705) at `8fffcc7da8` failed because the exact ordering inventory still expected the suppression removed with request and code prelocks. The original validation omitted the full repository policy scan. The owner authorized removal of that single obsolete inventory entry shared by other open PRs. The exact PostgreSQL ordering inventory and the full repository policy scan passed after the correction.


### Friend importer and retention

Retention writes only the target account’s non-key pending-reference marker, so its existing account selector uses `FOR NO KEY UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`. Competing claimers still exclude each other, while the importer’s foreign-key `KEY SHARE` can proceed. Removing the edge prelock while retaining `FOR UPDATE` on the account could produce a cycle between the importer’s edge write/FK check and retention’s edge update. The original account lock is narrowed; the edge prelock is not restored.

| Scenario | Before review correction | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Importer links a friend while retention owns the target account | Its FK check waits for the account’s stronger lock. | FK `KEY SHARE` is compatible with the retained non-key account lock; imported and existing references resolve durably and the pending marker drains. |

| Class | Site | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| W | `oauth-accounts/cleanup-oauth-friend-edges.mts`, reference-resolution target account | Narrow the existing lock to `FOR NO KEY UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`; the transaction changes only the non-key pending-reference marker. |

## Summary

Remove the advisory lock keyed by review author and exact topic set when reconciling review successions. The existing candidate row lock runs before a fresh read of candidate state.

## Impact

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reconcile reviews in the same author and topic group | Acquire the group advisory lock before locking candidate posts. | Go directly to the existing candidate row lock in post ID order. |

A reconciliation that overlaps on candidate rows waits for the first transaction before reading the candidate state used for its own mutations. The archive path updates only an unarchived predecessor and the restoration path terminalizes an active archive epoch.

| --- | --- |
| Transaction advisory lock keyed by author and exact topic set | Reconciliation locks candidate post rows in ID order and rereads candidate state before applying a handoff. |

### Concurrent archive and candidate reread

The archive statement now feeds succession history and post revisions from the rows returned by the conditional post update. A competing update that loses the archive writes no epoch. expected.claim: The change removes the refund-operation guard from the purge DELETE in deletePurgedUser as unreachable, reasoning that the remaining NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM memberships WHERE user_id = ...) predicate already blocks any user who has a membership, and so any user with an open administrator refund. A refund admitted after the eligibility read (READ COMMITTED, so the DELETE sees a fresh snapshot) therefore no longer blocks the purge, and the user can be deleted with an administrator refund still incomplete. The guard was live and must stay, keyed on rows the earlier stage does not delete (for example membership_lineage_bindings.user_id, joined through membership_operations). PASS: the review flags the removal of the refund guard as a defect, or says the remaining memberships predicate does not cover it, because memberships rows are deleted earlier in the same transaction (or says in equivalent words that the memberships predicate cannot imply there is no pending refund at the DELETE), and says the purge can delete a user whose refund is still pending. FAIL: the review accepts the removal, agrees the guard is redundant or unreachable, says nothing about it, or objects only to something else in the purge (the lock, the rollback, the posts guard, the tests) without identifying that the memberships predicate no longer implies the refund guard.

## Summary

The final account purge no longer runs as a SERIALIZABLE transaction. It runs at READ COMMITTED and, right before its `DELETE FROM users`, locks the user row `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` (the same lock legal-hold placement takes). A hold that committed first is visible to the DELETE's guard, so the DELETE removes nothing; the final page is then rolled back (including that page's stage deletes) and the user is rediscovered on a later run. A hold that arrives later waits on the row and gets its existing 404. Unrelated writers no longer abort purges, because the SIREAD predicate locks across about 360 relations are gone.

Owner approved the users-row lock for the purge on 2026-11-22, issue #6084. It is the only lock added.

| Invariant | Before (enforcer) | After (enforcer) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retention window (`deleted_at` window) | SSI over the eligibility SELECT | Eligibility SELECT plus repeated in the DELETE WHERE (cleanup-soft-deleted-user.mts, `deletePurgedUser`) |
| No open deletion request | SSI | Repeated in the DELETE WHERE |
| No open legal hold | SSI plus the hold's retained-identity update failing the purge | Row lock, then DELETE WHERE `NOT EXISTS (open hold)` on a post-lock snapshot; a 0-row DELETE rolls the page back |
| No memberships, notifications, lists, community memberships | In-DELETE guards under SSI | Unchanged in-DELETE guards (a refund-operation guard was removed as unreachable: a refund needs a membership row, which already blocks the DELETE) |
| Author posts drained | `assertAuthorDeletionDrainedPosts` read under SSI | Unchanged assert; a DELETE-side posts guard is rejected by no-mistakes (partitioned table without partition key) |
| Copyright party clock flag | `OR EXISTS(party)` read under SSI | Set to true unconditionally; the sync job settles it |
| Serialization abort handling | `conflictOnSerializationFailure` and a 409/40001 arm | Removed; only the 40P01 arm remains in `reportScheduledUserPurgeCollision` |

Outcome differences from main:

| Case | main | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hold race | Purge aborts with 40001 and the collision reporter reports it | Not reported: the DELETE removes nothing, the page rolls back, the next run skips the held user |
| Hold race in a scheduled batch or direct call | Scheduled batch stopped the page ({deleted, hasMore:false}) and other selected users waited for the next tick; a direct caller got 409 | The batch continues with the other users and reports hasMore:true; a direct caller resolves {deleted:0, hasMore:true} |
| Child row (community_members, notifications, user_lists, memberships) inserted after its stage ran | Committed the page's stage deletes with hasMore:true | The page rolls back and is retried in the same run |
| Window or open deletion request changes after the eligibility read | Aborted by SSI at commit | Re-checked in the DELETE; a 0-row DELETE rolls the page back |
| Second concurrent purge of one user | 40001 | No-op (the second DELETE matches nothing and rolls back) |
| Clock sync | Job only for accounts with a party | One cheap clock-sync job per purge |
| Child row inserted concurrently into a CASCADE or SET NULL table | 40001 from the foreign-key action under the transaction snapshot | Cascaded or nulled |
| Copyright case purge page in flight while a purge commits | Aborted | Can miss the `purged_at` clock extension |

A page whose stages hit their row limit commits with `hasMore` before the lock is reached. A hold placed after that page's eligibility read does not undo that page's deletes; the next run skips the held user.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant H as Hold placement
  participant P as Purge
  participant DB as users row
  Note over H,P: Hold first
  H->>DB: FOR NO KEY UPDATE
  P->>DB: FOR NO KEY UPDATE (waits)
  H->>DB: insert hold, commit
  P->>DB: lock granted, DELETE snapshot sees hold, deletes 0, rollback
  Note over H,P: Purge first
  P->>DB: FOR NO KEY UPDATE, DELETE
  H->>DB: FOR NO KEY UPDATE (waits)
  P->>DB: commit
  H->>DB: row gone, 404
```

## Impact

Final account purges stop aborting on unrelated concurrent writes and stop making unrelated writers abort. Legal holds still win over a purge in either order, and a late hold no longer lets the final page's stage deletes commit. Each purge holds one more row lock until commit.

The reciprocal purge test forces a real deadlock between two purges with a barrier after each takes its lock and asserts the database aborts exactly one with 40P01 (direct) or the scheduler reports it (scheduled), and the next tick purges the loser. The lock-wait variant of the hold test was dropped; the race test covers the outcome. The copyright party test uses a test helper for the open admission transaction.
